### Observed differences

- Activity A08 is no longer observed: in the earlier window it appeared in about 70 in 100 traces (141 of 200, averaging roughly 1.1 occurrences per trace), while in the later window it appears in none of the 200 traces. [OCC007, POS008]
- The fixed step A07 → A08 disappeared and its role moved up to A07: before, all 219 observed outgoing transitions of A07 led to A08; in the later window A07 leads instead to A05 (about 39 in 100 transitions), A03 (27), A04 (22) and A02 (12) — nearly the same mix A08 itself showed before (about 36, 35, 19 and 10 in 100). [DIR007, DIR008]
- Case-ending behaviour shifted from A08 to A07: before, about half of A08's ~219 occurrences ended the case (109 outgoing transitions) while A07 always had a successor; in the later window A07 has only about 97 outgoing transitions for ~201 occurrences, so it now ends the case about half the time. [DIR007, DIR008, OCC006, OCC007]
- The tight A07–A08 coupling is broken throughout: before, A07 and A08 always occurred together (co-occurrence in about 70 in 100 traces, never one without the other); in the later window A07 still appears in about 67 in 100 traces but never together with A08, and the same co-occurrence-to-zero pattern holds between A08 and each of A01, A02, A03, A04, A05, A06 and A09. [REL034, REL007, REL014, REL020, REL025, REL029, REL032, REL036]
- Smaller shifts are consistent with cases becoming one event shorter: A04 and A05 appear in somewhat fewer cases (75 → 63 and 72 → 66 of 200) and earlier within them, A06 appears later (mean relative position about 0.55 → 0.62), and step distances from A07 to its followers compressed (A02 followed A07 about 3 steps later in roughly 65 of 100 pair occurrences before, now within 1–2 steps). [POS004, POS005, POS006, LAG050, LAG053]
- Participation otherwise moved only slightly: A01 and A09 each appear a little more often (129 → 133 of 200 traces) and A07 a little less often (141 → 134). [OCC001, OCC008, OCC006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A08 was removed from the flow (or at least is no longer executed). In the earlier window, A08 ran in about 70 in 100 cases, always immediately after A07, and then either passed the case on to A05, A03, A04 or A02 (about 36, 35, 19 and 10 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) or ended the case (about half of its occurrences). In the later window, A08 does not occur at all, while A07 now passes cases directly to A05, A03, A04 and A02 in almost the same proportions and itself ends the case about half the time — the role A08 used to play. The change is observed directly on A08 (participation 141 → 0 of 200 traces; outgoing transitions 109 → 0) and on A07's successor profile (100% to A08 before, 0% after), and eight relation items independently show A08 co-occurring with no other activity any more; all of these items exceed 199 of 200 random re-splits, and a fall from 70% participation to zero across 200 traces is far beyond ordinary sampling variation. [OCC007, DIR007, DIR008, POS008, REL007, REL014, REL020, REL025, REL029, REL032, REL034, REL036]

What the evidence cannot rule out is a recording-level explanation — for example A08 being renamed or its events no longer being logged — which would look identical to removal here; the evidence shows only that A08 is not executed in the later traces, not why. [OCC007, DIR008]

Other differences: small shifts elsewhere are plausibly knock-on effects of cases becoming one event shorter rather than independent changes: A01 and A09 appear slightly more often (129 → 133 of 200 traces each) and A07, A04 and A05 slightly less often (141 → 134, 75 → 63 and 72 → 66); A06 sits later in the case (mean relative position about 0.55 → 0.62) while A04 and A05 sit earlier; and step-distance distributions shifted for many activity pairs, generally compressing (for example A06 → A04 moved from mostly 4 steps apart to 2–3 steps), though several of these lag items rest on fewer than about 30 pair observations. None of these involves an activity appearing or disappearing. [OCC001, OCC008, OCC006, OCC004, POS006, POS004, POS005, LAG044, LAG012]
